current_example.problem: Solve the equation $\dfrac{xy}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2}$ for the variable $y.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We need to isolate all terms with $y$ on one side of the equation. To do this, we first cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{xy}{3} & =\frac{y-1}{2} \\ 2\cdot xy & =3\cdot (y-1) \\ 2xy & =3y-3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we subtract $3y$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy & =3y-3 \\ 2xy-3y & =3y-3-3y \\ 2xy-3y & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that all terms containing $y$ are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of $y$ are on the right-hand side.

Then, we factor out $y$ from the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy-3y & =-3 \\ y(2x-3) & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides by $(2x - 3)$ to isolate $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(2x-3) & =-3 \\ \frac{y(2x-3)}{2x-3} & =\frac{-3}{2x-3} \\ \frac{y\cancel{(2x-3)}}{\cancel{2x-3}} & =\frac{-3}{2x-3} \\ y & =-\frac{3}{2x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** This result assumes that $2x-3\neq 0.$
